transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I’m Dr. [Your Name]. Can you tell me what’s been going on that brought you in today?

Um, thanks, Doctor. I guess I came in because I’ve been getting… kind of stuck on things more than I think is normal. It’s not that I’m trying to waste time, but I’ll reread emails or texts over and over, reopen folders on my computer, and sometimes replay conversations in my head before I leave the house or start work.

I keep feeling like I need to make sure I didn’t miss something or make some serious mistake. It probably sounds a little silly, but it’s been taking up chunks of time, and I thought I should maybe talk to someone about it.
Do you find yourself having thoughts that come up over and over again that you don’t really want, that bother you or make you feel anxious?

Yes… I think so. I don’t want to make it sound more dramatic than it is, but even when I’m trying to focus on work — like working through a system design or preparing a lesson — I’ll get this thought barging in that maybe I sent the wrong message to my ex-wife, or mishandled some family photos, or somehow let someone in the community down.

And I know, rationally, I’ve already gone over it. But it doesn’t really feel settled, if that makes sense. It just keeps coming back and makes me anxious until I check or think it through again.
When these anxious thoughts come up, do you feel driven to do something — like checking, counting, or repeating actions — to try to reduce the anxiety or prevent something bad from happening?

Yes… I think “driven” is probably the right word, though I don’t love admitting that.

It’s mostly checking and rechecking. I’ll reread emails or texts several times, reopen folders on my computer just to make sure I didn’t miss something, and I’ll go back over conversations in my head before I leave the house or start work. It’s like I’m trying to prove to myself that I didn’t make some serious mistake.

I know that may sound excessive, and I can usually tell myself it’s probably fine, but if I don’t do it, I feel unsettled and distracted. Then I end up losing chunks of time to it.
